blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Logistics means connecting cities. Every shipment starts in one place and ends in another. We use two small words: from and to. "From" is the origin. "To" is the destination.

Today we describe real Czarnikow routes. The sugar goes from Santos to London. It goes from Brazil to Europe. It goes from the mill to the customer.

When you say "from A to B", you describe a route. Clear origin and destination means no confused deliveries. A good shipment always starts in one place and ends in the right place.

items.q: What word do we use for the origin?
items.why: "'From' is the origin." From = origem.

items.q: Where does the sugar go, in the example?
options: From the customer to the mill
items.why: "The sugar goes from Santos to London."

items.q: What does "to" mean?
items.why: "'To' is the destination." To = destino.

items.q: The text suggests that a clear origin and destination helps because…
items.why: Inferência: "Clear origin and destination means no confused deliveries."

items.q: The author would most likely AGREE that…
options: London is the origin of the sugar
every shipment stays in one city
a route needs both a start and an end
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo mostra que uma rota vai de um ponto (from) a outro (to).

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando a rota ao cliente novo. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hello, and welcome. Thank you for your first order. Let me explain the route of your sugar. It is very simple.

First, the sugar comes from the mill. The mill is in Brazil, near the fields. Then a truck takes it to the port. Our port is Santos. Santos is a big port on the coast.

At the port, we put the sugar on a ship. The ship is big and slow, but it is safe. It carries many bags. The ship goes from Brazil to Europe. This trip takes about three weeks.

The destination is London. In London, we take the sugar off the ship. Then a truck takes it from the port to you, the customer. So the full route is: from the mill, to the port, to the ship, to London, to you.

Please always check the origin and the destination on your paperwork. If both are clear, there are no problems. Do you have any questions? I am happy to help.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Where does the sugar come from first?
items.why: "First, the sugar comes from the mill."

items.q: Which port does James name?
items.why: "Our port is Santos."

items.q: How long does the ship trip take?
items.why: "The ship goes from Brazil to Europe. This trip takes about three weeks."

items.q: James suggests that the customer should…
options: send the sugar back to Santos
check the origin and destination on the paperwork
items.why: Inferência: "Please always check the origin and the destination on your paperwork."

items.q: How would you describe James's tone?
items.why: Inferência: ele dá boas-vindas, explica com calma e se oferece para ajudar.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The origin of the sugar is Brazil." Origin means…
items.why: Origin = origem, o ponto de partida.

items.q: "London is the final destination." Destination means…
items.why: Destination = destino, onde a carga termina.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The truck takes the sugar to the ___, and there we put it on a ship."
items.why: Port = porto, onde o navio espera a carga.

items.q: "We ship the sugar to Europe every month." Here, to ship means…
items.why: To ship = enviar (também pode ser o substantivo "navio").

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Brazil is a big ___ in South America."
items.why: Country = país. Brazil é um país.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas de logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The ship goes to London via the Atlantic." Via means…
items.why: Via = passando por, indo através de um lugar.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the shipment." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new route next month." To roll out means to…
options: start it and put it into use
items.why: Roll out = colocar em uso, lançar.

items.q: "The customer pushed back on the delivery date." This means the customer…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "Please follow up on the order and tell me when it arrives." To follow up on means to…
items.why: Follow up on = dar sequência, verificar de novo depois.
